## What changed

- Open on a single concrete failure scene: a frontier agent reading a treasury bond, "$10,000" rendered as "$3,000," a downstream agent acting on the wrong number (Databricks example).
- Establish the core thesis: *the bottleneck for agent quality in 2026 is not reasoning — it is reading.*
- One-sentence definition of "agentic OCR" to anchor the rest of the book (full definition lives in Chapter 3).

## Why 2026 matters

- Cite the **67% adoption** number — enterprises evaluating agentic vs. classic IDP, up from 23% two years prior.
- Note the structural forcing functions: CMS prior-auth transparency rule (March 2026), enterprise consolidation to one or two vendors per workflow, capital concentration.
- Land the point that this book exists because the field crossed a threshold this year — vocabulary, vendor stability, and benchmark maturity are simultaneously sufficient.

## Who this book is for

- Two readers, one book. Implementers and decision-makers, sharing each chapter.
- Each chapter opens with an executive callout; the technical body follows.
- Skip-paths: foundations for newcomers, Part III for buyers, Part IV for integrators, Part V first for skeptics.

## How to read this book

- Five parts. Linear but skippable.
- Pointer to glossary, cheatsheet, and bibliography in the appendices.
- One paragraph on what the book is *not* — not a tutorial, not vendor-neutral, not stable forever.

## Named take

> *"If your agent can read perfectly but reason imperfectly, you have a model problem. If your agent reasons brilliantly on the wrong inputs, you have a document problem — and 2026 says the document problem is bigger."*
